top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a distinct invention, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, that took fractional uncertainty to about 1e-18. It has been reproduced and surpassed independently at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE, and it now yields physics (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, limits on constants and dark-matter couplings). The two-name allocation is short and was proposed identically by all eight members, and the citation names the invention and its performance, separating it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The attribution gap to Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Bloom and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups is real but does not justify withholding the prize.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no connection to the optical lattice clock groups, though as an experimental instrument builder I am sympathetic to detector and measurement-technique work
